question_pattern: Is the vendor's service supporting a critical or important function?
approved_answer: Classification is the financial entity's decision. We provide the inputs it needs: service description, dependencies, sub-processor list and recovery objectives (RTO 4h, RPO 15 min for the EU tenant).
reuse_note: Never answer 'not critical' on the client's behalf.

question_pattern: Provide information for the client's register of information.
approved_answer: We supply the register fields as a structured annex: legal entity details, LEI, service type, data locations, sub-processors with country and function, and contract dates.
reuse_note: Fill the annex per client; do not paste a generic list.

approved_answer: Full export of all fund, investor and document data in documented open formats within 30 days of request, a transition period of up to 12 months on existing terms, and certified deletion within 30 days after exit.
evidence: MSA DORA addendum §9; export format spec

question_pattern: What are your ICT incident notification commitments?
approved_answer: Initial notice to the client within 4 hours of classifying an incident affecting its service, intermediate update within 24 hours and root-cause report within 30 days, so the client can meet its own reporting deadlines.
evidence: Incident response runbook; MSA DORA addendum §6
reuse_note: Our clock is contractual; the client's regulatory reporting clock is its own.

question_pattern: Do you participate in the client's resilience testing and TLPT?
approved_answer: Yes. We participate in the client's ICT testing on 60 days' notice and in pooled or client-led TLPT where the client's competent authority requires it, subject to agreed scope and rules of engagement.

question_pattern: State the locations where data is processed and stored.
approved_answer: EU tenant data is stored and processed in AWS eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) across three availability zones, including backups, snapshots, search indexes, logs and LLM inference. Remote support access from outside the EEA is described in GDPR-19.
reuse_note: Re-verify the egress policy before every reuse.

question_pattern: Can the client and its competent authority audit and inspect the vendor?
approved_answer: Yes: unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit for the client, its appointed auditors and its competent authority, plus pooled audits on request; SOC 2 Type II report available annually.
evidence: MSA DORA addendum §7; SOC 2 Type II report

question_pattern: How are subcontractors supporting the service controlled?
approved_answer: Each sub-processor is listed with country and function; changes are notified 30 days in advance with a right to object; the same DORA obligations flow down in writing.

question_pattern: What categories of LP personal data are processed?
approved_answer: Identification and contact data, tax identifiers, beneficial ownership details, PEP and sanctions screening results, bank account details and signatures of investors, signatories and controlling persons.

question_pattern: Is personal data transferred outside the EEA?
approved_answer: Data at rest and in processing stays in eu-central-1. The only transfer is just-in-time support access (GDPR-19), covered by the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914) and a transfer impact assessment.
reuse_note: Never answer 'no transfers' if support staff outside the EEA can view data.

question_pattern: Can support staff outside the EU view LP personal data?
approved_answer: Only through just-in-time sessions approved per ticket, with LP personal data masked by default. Unmasking needs a client-approved ticket, is time-boxed to 4 hours and is logged. Remote viewing is treated as a transfer and covered under GDPR-11.
evidence: Support access policy; access logs sample

question_pattern: Does any LP personal data leave eu-central-1 for AI inference?
approved_answer: No. EU tenant LLM calls go only to the AI provider's EU (Frankfurt) region endpoint; the EU VPC denies egress to any non-allow-listed endpoint.
reuse_note: This answer was 'No' only after the September 2025 changes. Re-verify.

question_pattern: Confirm zero retention and no training on client data by AI providers.
approved_answer: The AI provider processes prompts and outputs under contractual zero-data-retention terms, with no use of client data for training or model improvement, flowed down in its DPA.
reuse_note: Quote the contract; never paraphrase a vendor's marketing page.

question_pattern: Can AI features be disabled for the client's tenant?
approved_answer: Yes. AI features are off by default for EU tenants and enabled per tenant by the client's administrator; disabling them stops all AI sub-processor calls.

question_pattern: Provide your latest independent assurance report.
approved_answer: SOC 2 Type II covering Security, Availability and Confidentiality for a 12-month period, with bridge letter for the gap to the current date.
evidence: SOC 2 Type II report under NDA
reuse_note: Check the report period before quoting it.

question_pattern: How is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
approved_answer: AES-256 at rest with keys in AWS KMS in eu-central-1, which cannot be used from other regions; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit; per-tenant encryption keys for the document store.
